meta.purpose: Classification hints used by scripts/check-privacy.mjs to sort what a page sets or requests before consent.
meta.caution: Host names and cookie names below are illustrations of common properties, not a list of unlawful vendors. A purpose cannot be known from a name: a match is a reason to look, and a site states its exempt trackers in compliance/trackers.json. Whether a given setup needs consent depends on its purpose and configuration.

verdicts.non-exempt: Reported as a non-conformity when present before consent or after refusal.
verdicts.to-review: Reported as a point to review: the purpose may or may not be exempt.

host_categories.label: Advertising and ad measurement
host_categories.why: Hosts that serve or measure advertising usually read or write an identifier to recognise the same browser across several sites; advertising is not among the exempt purposes.

host_categories.label: Social network pixels and plugins
host_categories.why: Pixels and share or like plugins loaded from a social network let that network link the visit to its own identifiers, including for people who are not members.

host_categories.label: Audience measurement on a vendor's infrastructure
host_categories.why: Exemption of audience measurement requires conditions that a checker cannot verify from the browser (measurement for the publisher's exclusive account, anonymous statistics only, no cross-site tracking, no transmission to third parties). Libraries and loaders served from these hosts usually set a persistent identifier.

host_categories.label: Session replay and heatmaps
host_categories.why: Session replay records the user's interactions with the page; the CNIL requires prior consent for it.

host_categories.label: Audience measurement that can be configured for exemption
host_categories.why: Some measurement tools can be configured to meet the exemption conditions, or work without storing anything on the terminal; the configuration decides, and it is not visible from the browser.

host_categories.label: Embedded players and maps
host_categories.why: Embedded players and maps load content from a third party that may read or write identifiers; a click-to-load placeholder avoids the request before consent.

host_categories.label: Font services and public code hosting
host_categories.why: No identifier is expected, but each request transmits the visitor's IP address to a third party, and code hosted elsewhere can change without notice; self-hosting avoids both.

storage_name_patterns.why: Name used by a widespread analytics library for a persistent browser identifier.
Names used by analytics libraries for visitor or session identifiers and throttling.
Names used by advertising and conversion measurement to recognise the browser.
Names used by social network pixels to link the visit to the network's identifiers.
Names used by session replay and heatmap tools.
Names used by product analytics libraries for a persistent identifier.
Names used by a measurement tool that can be configured to meet the exemption conditions; the configuration decides.

exempt_name_hints.why: The name suggests storage of the user's choice about trackers, an exempt purpose if it stores nothing else.
The name suggests a session, authentication or anti-forgery token, exempt if strictly needed for a service the user asked for.
The name suggests a shopping basket, an exempt purpose.
The name suggests an interface preference the user expects to be kept (language, display), an exempt purpose.
The name suggests load balancing or traffic routing, an exempt purpose.
